title: The game loop
summary: Fixed timestep: the same physics on a slow phone and a fast one.

cards.title: Variable frames, fixed physics
cards.body:
Rendered frames take different times: 8 ms on a flagship, 50 ms on an old phone. If physics advanced by "however long the frame took", jumps would reach different heights on different devices.

**Fixed timestep**: bank the real time in an accumulator, then advance the simulation in steps of exactly `dt`.
Change the frame times in the Algorithm Lab to see when 0, 1 or several updates happen.
`alpha` says how far we are between two simulation states, so rendering can blend them and stay smooth even with a 20 ms physics tick.

cards.question: dt = 20 ms. The accumulator holds 5 ms and the next frame takes 37 ms. How many updates run?
cards.explain: 5 + 37 = 42 ms banked: two 20 ms steps (40 ms), 2 ms carried to the next frame.
